findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the classification procedure that maps a carried standing item to still-present / addressed / withdrawn (what input each state keys off, e.g. cited-location diff vs presence in fresh Pass-1).
evidence: 'Each item is recorded still-present, addressed, or withdrawn on a new standing sub-object'
Testing: 'cited lines deleted -> addressed; ... rebase-only -> all kept' — outcomes stated, mechanism absent
No bullet describes how 'addressed' is distinguished from 'withdrawn' or 'still-present'
findings.finding: The procedure for deciding a standing item's state (still-present / addressed / withdrawn) is not specified. Testing lists 'cited lines deleted -> addressed' and 'rebase-only -> all kept' as expected outcomes, but the Approach never describes HOW the system classifies an item into these three states (e.g. by diffing cited locations against the new revision, by presence in fresh Pass-1, etc.). An executor cannot implement the classifier from the plan alone.
scenarios: Executor must guess whether 'addressed' means the cited source lines were deleted, the finding was re-emitted by fresh Pass-1, or something else
'withdrawn' has no described trigger at all
findings.suggested_fix: Add a State-decision sub-bullet: e.g. 'addressed' = the item's cited location(s) no longer exist in revision N's diff; 'still-present' = location survives and fresh Pass-1 did not re-emit; 'withdrawn' = <defined trigger>.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how each `standing.state` (still-present/addressed/withdrawn) is computed and at which stage: name the data (diff/deps) the computing stage receives, and reconcile with `merge_findings` having no region/diff access — or move state computation to a stage that does.
evidence: Plan: 'Each item is recorded still-present, addressed, or withdrawn on a new standing sub-object ({origin_revision, state})' with no computation rule
merge_findings body (workflow_ops.py:237-257) only reads finding lists (base/round_a/round_b or `sources`); no diff/deps/repo_root region access
region_for_finding docstring (region_gate.py:34-43): returns REGION_UNCHANGED/CHANGED/UNKNOWN at file content-hash level — no line-deletion signal
Testing case 'cited lines deleted -> addressed' presupposes line-granularity detection the named tools do not provide
findings.finding: The tri-state (still-present/addressed/withdrawn) recorded on the new `standing` sub-object has no specified computation mechanism, and the named injection stage cannot produce it: `merge_findings` (workflow_ops.py:237-257) is a pure concatenate+cluster op that receives only finding LISTS — it has no diff, no `prior_deps`, and no region access — yet the plan injects `standing` there and the Testing section requires 'cited lines deleted -> addressed' and 'rebase-only -> all kept'. The only named region tool, `region_gate.region_for_finding` (region_gate.py:31-43), classifies at FILE-CONTENT-HASH granularity (REGION_UNCHANGED/CHANGED/UNKNOWN) and cannot distinguish a deleted cited LINE (addressed) from a changed-but-still-applicable finding (still-present vs withdrawn).
findings.location: Approach > State; Scope (merge_findings :226); Testing (cited lines deleted -> addressed)
scenarios: A carried finding cites path:120; PS N deletes lines 100-130 — plan wants `addressed`, but region_for_finding only says REGION_CHANGED for the whole file, not that line 120 vanished
Implementer wires state at merge_findings and has no diff to compute anything but a constant state
findings.suggested_fix: Compute `state` where diff+prior_deps are available (e.g. the carry_forward helper called with `diff_text`/`prior_deps`, alongside `region_for_finding`), not in `merge_findings`; define `still-present` = fresh Pass-1 re-emitted the norm_id, `addressed`/`withdrawn` = derived from region + a line-level check, and pass the resolved `standing` object into merge_findings as data.

findings.checklist_item: State the termination/anti-ratchet invariant for carried standing items (what makes this a one-shot backstop, not a permanent ratchet), and justify why region-gating + grounded-only suffices without plan-review's material-unchanged suppression guard.
evidence: plan_review sidecar.py:436-443: 'When the ticket's material has CHANGED since the prior review... replaying it verbatim is memory, not review. So a prior sidecar whose material_fingerprint differs... suppresses recall entirely.'

Plan carries only the grounded-only guard ('carried evidence terminates the chain') — the evidence-less guard breaks the RECALL ratchet in plan-review, but here items carry state across patchsets by design
Testing: 'rebase-only -> all kept' — carried items survive a rebase, the exact scenario where material may differ
findings.finding: The plan claims to MIRROR plan-review's recall backstop ('no second mechanism') but drops one of that mechanism's two anti-ratchet eligibility guards without an equivalent termination argument. plan_review.prior_concerns gates on grounded-only AND material-UNCHANGED (`_material_changed`, sidecar.py:423-443), where a changed fingerprint SUPPRESSES recall entirely so a fixed finding cannot replay forever. The plan ports grounded-only but replaces material-unchanged with region-gating, and the 'rebase-only -> all kept' test shows standing items persist across patchsets. The plan never states how the carry-forward chain TERMINATES for a finding whose region keeps churning yet is never re-emitted — i.e., why this is a one-shot backstop and not the permanent ratchet plan-review's material-changed guard was added to prevent.
findings.location: Approach ('Mirror plan-review's recall backstop — no second mechanism'); Approach > Grounded-only; Testing (rebase-only -> all kept)
scenarios: A finding cites a region that churns every patchset but the fresh finder never re-raises it — does it carry forward on PS3, PS4, PS5... indefinitely, blocking merge on stale grounding?
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit rule that a standing item marked `addressed`/`withdrawn` (or whose region is REGION_CHANGED with no re-emit) is NOT re-carried on the next patchset, mirroring plan-review's material-changed suppression, and document it beside the grounded-only rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the assignment rule for every `standing.state` value, including the deterministic trigger that distinguishes `withdrawn` from `addressed` (or drop `withdrawn` if it has no path).
evidence: State: 'Each item is recorded `still-present`, `addressed`, or `withdrawn` on a new `standing` sub-object'
Testing maps only: 'cited lines deleted -> `addressed`' and 'rebase-only -> all kept' (still-present); no case exercises or triggers `withdrawn`
search_files for `withdrawn` under src/rebar/llm/code_review returns (no matches) — the value is net-new and has no existing precedent to infer its rule from
Acceptance test `sidecar_records_standing_state` asserts `standing.state` exists but the plan gives no rule to decide which of the three the executor must emit
findings.finding: The `standing.state` enum defines three values (`still-present`, `addressed`, `withdrawn`) but only two have an assignment rule; `withdrawn` has no defined trigger anywhere in the plan.
scenarios: An executor implementing the state stamp in merge_findings cannot decide when a dropped-and-not-re-emitted finding is `withdrawn` vs `addressed`
A reviewer reading the Gerrit message ('since patchset k') cannot know what `withdrawn` communicates vs `addressed`
findings.suggested_fix: State the trigger for each value co-located with the definition, e.g. `addressed` = a cited location was deleted/changed by the diff; `withdrawn` = the finding's criterion is no longer routed/enabled for this change (the 1867 'defect changed criterion' case); `still-present` = the cited region is unchanged (rebase-only).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Co-locate the standing-state assignment with the diff/deletion signal it needs, naming the exact step (and its inputs) that computes each state.
evidence: Plan: 'Items whose `norm_id` fresh Pass-1 did not produce are appended by `merge_findings` (`workflow_ops.py:226`)' and State: recorded '`still-present`, `addressed`, or `withdrawn`'

merge_findings (workflow_ops.py:237-257, read) only concatenates sources, clusters near-duplicates, and assigns a 0-based `id`; it receives no diff_text/deleted-lines input (that DET signal is enriched later in _det_enrich_verifications / code_review_decide, workflow_ops.py:418-425)
The `addressed` state per Testing requires knowing 'cited lines deleted' — a diff signal merge_findings is not shown to have
findings.finding: The state-assignment decision rule is not co-located with the component that produces it: the plan injects standing items and stamps `standing` in `merge_findings`, but merge_findings is a deterministic cluster+id step with no diff/deletion input, and the plan never says which signal it reads to compute the state.
findings.location: Approach > Injection point / State; Scope > workflow_ops.py
scenarios: Executor writes the state computation in merge_findings but has no diff/deletion data there, forcing an unplanned data-flow change or a wrong-place stamp
A cited-lines-deleted finding cannot be marked `addressed` at the injection seam because the deletion signal arrives at a later step
findings.suggested_fix: Either pass the diff/deletion signal into merge_findings explicitly, or move the state stamp to the step that already has it (the DET-enrich path near code_review_decide), and state which inputs each state reads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback `standing.state` (and any coverage/observability stamp) when the deletion/rebase signal cannot be resolved.
evidence: prior_concerns (plan_review/sidecar.py:445-465, read) is 'best-effort and NEVER raises' with named degrade outcomes ('a missing one leaves recall enabled', 'coverage["recall_suppressed"]' reasons)

The plan's State section names the three outcomes but no default/fallback when the signal that picks among them is missing (e.g. a location-less finding, or a finding whose cited path is unresolvable in the diff)
Plan asserts it mirrors the backstop ('no second mechanism') yet omits the analogue's degrade specification for the state field
findings.finding: No fallback state is specified for a standing item when the deletion/rebase signal is unresolvable, unlike the plan-review recall analogue which the plan claims to mirror and which specifies explicit best-effort degrade paths.
scenarios: A carried finding with no `location` (location-less clustered finding) reaches the state stamp with no diff anchor to test deletion
The diff read fails or the cited path is renamed — the executor has no defined state to emit
findings.suggested_fix: Name a conservative default (e.g. `still-present`, matching the posture clamp's 'cannot raise' stance) for the unresolvable-signal case, and record the reason in coverage as prior_concerns does.

evidence: 4 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State STANDING_CAP's default value (or derive it, e.g. mirror plan-review's cap) in the plan rather than deferring the choice to the executor.
evidence: 'Capped by STANDING_CAP.'
Scope: 'standing_items(), STANDING_CAP' — named but never assigned a value
No default or derivation given
findings.finding: STANDING_CAP is introduced as the cap governing how many prior findings are carried, but no value or derivation is stated anywhere in the plan. The reader 'Capped by STANDING_CAP' and the Scope lists the symbol, yet its magnitude is left to the executor.
scenarios: Executor must pick an arbitrary cap; too low silently drops carried findings, too high bloats the payload
findings.suggested_fix: State the concrete cap value, ideally matched to plan-review's recall-backstop cap for consistency with the mirrored mechanism.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the plan-review injection-seam citation from `pass1.py:373-374` to `pass1.py:488-510` (the `prior_concerns` -> norm_id-match -> `findings.append(..., evidence, _recall)` block).
evidence: Plan: "Items whose `norm_id` fresh Pass-1 did not produce are appended by `merge_findings` (`workflow_ops.py:226`), flowing into `code_review_verify_inputs` (`:262`) — plan-review's seam (`pass1.py:373-374`)"
pass1.py:368-373 is the cache-warm block: `warm = (bool(chunks) and _prefix_tokens(plan) >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS ...)` / `warmed = False` — observability, not recall

pass1.py:488-510 is the actual seam: `concerns = sidecar.prior_concerns(...)`, `seen = {sidecar.norm_id(f) for f in findings}`, and `findings.append({... 'evidence': list(c.get('evidence') or []), '_recall': True})` when `nid not in seen`
findings.finding: The plan cites plan-review's recall/injection seam — the pattern this whole plan mirrors ('Items whose norm_id fresh Pass-1 did not produce are appended... plan-review's seam') — at pass1.py:373-374, but that location is cache-warming batch observability (the warm/warmed flag). The actual seam that matches missed findings by norm_id and appends them with carried evidence is pass1.py:488-510 (sidecar.prior_concerns -> seen-set by norm_id -> findings.append with evidence).
findings.location: Approach -> 'Injection point' bullet; Scope -> workflow_ops.py merge_findings inject
scenarios: An implementer opens pass1.py:373-374 to mirror the seam and finds cache-warming code, not the norm_id-match-and-append the plan is describing

findings.checklist_item: Correct the posture-clamp threshold/criteria_routing.json attribution to registry.effective_routing / registry.threshold_for (workflow_ops.py:426-430) and registry.py's criteria_routing.json rather than workflow_ops.py:423.
evidence: Plan: 'the threshold resolved per criterion from criteria_routing.json (workflow_ops.py:423) where eight criteria are blocking_enabled: true'
workflow_ops.py:423 is `diff_text=str(ctx.inputs.get("diff_text") or "")` inside _det_enrich_verifications
workflow_ops.py:426-430: routing = registry.effective_routing(ctx.repo_root); threshold_for=lambda criteria: registry.threshold_for(criteria, routing)
registry.py:144 `_ROUTING_RESOURCE = "criteria_routing.json"` — the routing/blocking_enabled resolution lives in registry.py
findings.finding: The posture-clamp mechanism attributes per-criterion threshold resolution and the criteria_routing.json 'blocking_enabled' map to workflow_ops.py:423, but :423 is the diff_text argument to _det_enrich_verifications; the threshold actually resolves via registry.effective_routing / registry.threshold_for (workflow_ops.py:426-430) and criteria_routing.json is owned by llm/code_review/registry.py, not workflow_ops.py.
scenarios: Implementer building code_review_decide's clamp follows the citation to workflow_ops.py:423 to find the threshold source and finds only a diff_text arg, not the blocking_enabled routing.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-anchor the sentence to 'the threshold resolved per criterion from criteria_routing.json via registry.threshold_for (workflow_ops.py:426-430)'.
